finding: Placental pathology was more common in pathological pregnancies (73.8%) compared to normal pregnancies (26.2%), and while neonatal health status was associated with pregnancy outcome, some pathological infants were born from normal pregnancies and vice versa.
mod_finding: The majority of normal pregnancies (most of which had undergone elective cesarean section for maternal or fetal indication) had a normal placenta (57.5%).
